1	# Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks: Time Horizon Doubling Every 7 Months
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	- URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499
     5	- Authors: Thomas Kwa, Ben West, Joel Becker, et al. — Model Evaluation & Threat Research (METR)
     6	- Published: March 2025
     7	
     8	## The Time Horizon Metric
     9	
    10	The paper proposes a new metric for quantifying AI autonomous capabilities: the **50% task-completion time horizon** — the duration of tasks (measured by how long they take skilled human professionals) that an AI model can complete with 50% success rate. This provides an intuitive, human-grounded measure of real-world AI capability that allows comparison across vastly different models (e.g., GPT-2 vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet).
    11	
    12	The methodology involves three steps: (1) assembling a diverse suite of 170 software/research tasks, (2) timing skilled humans and measuring AI agent success rates on these tasks, and (3) fitting a logistic model to estimate the task duration at which each AI agent achieves 50% success.
    13	
    14	![Methodology overview](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    15	
    16	## Task Suite: 170 Tasks from 1 Second to 8 Hours
    17	
    18	The benchmark combines three task suites: HCAST (97 diverse software tasks, 1 min–30 hrs), RE-Bench (7 difficult ML research engineering tasks, all 8 hrs), and Software Atomic Actions / SWAA (66 short single-step tasks, 1 sec–30 sec). Over 800 human baselines totaling 2,529 hours were collected.
    19	
    20	| Family | Human Time | Description |
    21	|---|---|---|
    22	| find_shell_script | 3 seconds | Multiple choice: "Which file is a shell script?" |
    23	| wikipedia_research | 1 minute | Research simple factual information from Wikipedia |
    24	| oxdna_simple | 9 minutes | Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files |
    25	| munge_data | 56 minutes | Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules |
    26	| cuda_backtesting | 8 hours | Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30x speedup of a backtesting tool |
    27	
    28	## Exponential Growth in AI Time Horizon (2019–2025)
    29	
    30	The central finding is that the 50% time horizon has grown exponentially from 2019 to 2025, with a **doubling time of approximately 207 days (~7 months)** and an R² of 0.97. Key data points across models:
    31	
    32	| Model | Release Period | 50% Time Horizon |
    33	|---|---|---|
    34	| GPT-2 | 2019 | ~2 seconds |
    35	| GPT-3 (davinci-002) | 2020 | ~9 seconds |
    36	| GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct | 2023 | ~36 seconds |
    37	| GPT-4 (0314) | 2023 | ~5 minutes |
    38	| GPT-4o | 2024 | ~9 minutes |
    39	| Claude 3 Opus | 2024 | ~6 minutes |
    40	| Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New) | 2024 | ~28 minutes |
    41	| o1 | 2024 | ~39 minutes |
    42	| Claude 3.7 Sonnet | 2025 | ~54 minutes |
    43	| o3 | 2025 | ~1 hour 50 minutes |
    44	
    45	![Exponential trend in AI time horizon](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    46	
    47	The 2023–2025 growth rate is approximately 20% faster than the overall 2019–2025 rate, suggesting possible acceleration. The 80% time horizon (tasks completed 80% of the time) shows a similar trend but with horizons roughly 5x shorter.
    48	
    49	![Per-model success probability curves](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    50	
    51	## Drivers and Limitations
    52	
    53	Progress appears driven by: **improved logical reasoning**, **better tool use**, **greater reliability and self-awareness** in task execution, and **ability to adapt to mistakes**. However, performance is notably lower on less structured, "messier" tasks. External validity remains an open question — the tasks do not perfectly represent the average segment of real-world intellectual labor, though supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.
    54	
    55	## Key Findings
    56	
    57	- **50% time horizon** provides a robust, intuitive metric for tracking AI autonomous capability growth, with R² = 0.97 over 6 years of model releases.
    58	- Frontier AI agents (o3) can now autonomously complete tasks that take skilled humans **nearly 2 hours**, up from 2 seconds for GPT-2 in 2019.
    59	- The doubling time is **~7 months**, with possible acceleration since 2024.
    60	- Naive extrapolation predicts AI will reach a **1-month time horizon (167 work hours) between mid-2028 and mid-2031**, implying automation of many month-long software projects.
    61	- Key capability drivers are reasoning, tool use, and error recovery; key limitations include poor performance on unstructured tasks and uncertain external validity to real-world job distributions.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1

   146	#### Text Box

   164	#### Shapes

   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167

   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```

   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237

   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python

   261

   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'

   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)

   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   438	## Limitations

    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                font_color=TEXT_WHITE, bold=False, italic=False,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri", wrap=True):
    """Add a formatted text box to a slide."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.italic = italic
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                       font_size=Pt(14), font_color=TEXT_WHITE,
                       bullet_color=ACCENT_TEAL, font_name="Calibri",
                       line_spacing=1.2):
    """Add a text box with bullet paragraphs."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return txBox

    """Add a consistent dark header bar with title and optional subtitle."""
    # Header background
    header = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
        Inches(0), Inches(0),
        SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(1.15)
    )
    header.fill.solid()
    header.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARKER_BG
    header.line.fill.background()
    
    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.5),
                title_text, font_size=Pt(28), bold=True,
                font_color=TEXT_WHITE, font_name="Calibri Light")
